chapter: Road bands: Hucklebuck Williams and Tiny Bradshaw
title: First night with Bradshaw's band, Bill Hardman and Philip Paul
summary: Peck Morrison is leaving, Sam sits in at a packed gig, meets young Bill Hardman and Philip Paul, and finds the band hot.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Up there--150th Street between Broadway and Amsterdam and got my bag. And we split. And Peck Morrison was the bass player and, and, in Tiny Bradshaw's band but he was quitting because he had something to do here in New York.
Uh huh.
Something, or he didn't want to go on the road no more or something.
Uh huh.

And so Peck was--was playing his last gig so--well, the place was jam-packed with people, man. So I'm--you know, I've heard Bradshaw's band, you know. So I looked up there and I--in the band. I saw some guys up there my age--which was Bill Hardman what was in the band.
Uh huh.

And the drummer was Philip Paul. And I say "shit, yeah." You know, so ah, so Bradshaw told me--say "look. You on the payroll as of right now. Sit down and listen at the band and uh, you know, and just, you know, listen at the band, man. And, and, and hear them and get started like that, you know."
Yeah.
I say "fine, shit, man. I sit down and I'm getting paid for nothing, you know."
Yeah.
You know, and I listen to the band and them guys was hitting it, man, they sounded good, you know. Because his band wasn't uh--his band was a--wasn't no uh, uh, uh, what you call a commercial band.
Hmm.
So he, he--his band was what you call a swing band, you know. "Second Balcony.....". , you know.
Uh huh.
And uh, and he had the--his band was hot as fire, man. With "Heavy Juice" ....."Soft. V.....
Yeah.
That band was hot as fire, man.
Ooooh.
You know. And people was coming from all corners of the world to hear this band, you know.
Yeah.
And I said "God damn, boy. How'd I luck
up to get this gig, you know." And these people was looking for me, you know.
Uh huh.

And I'm saying this shit to myself, man. So I met Bill Hardman, you know. And he said "here man, I'm sure glad you're in the band." And I said "I'm glad too, man, because all the bands I've been in have been like grown--I'm the youngest dude in the band, you know."
Uh huh.
I'm glad to have somebody in there my age and stuff, you know.
Uh huh.

Me and him and Paul. So next night was my turn to play, you know. Say, you know, just luckily enough, man, all them songs they played I could play them, man. I, you know, shit. And I had--I had a pretty good instrument. And shit, my bass was singing, man. I--I was singing all through that stuff, man. Say Bradshaw like me too, you know.
Uh huh.
I say shit, I'm in, you know. Man thirty-five one-nighters and we were playing the Savoy Ballroom.
Uh huh.

And we were going the Apollo Theatre, we'd augment the band, the big bands. The Howard Theatre, and the theatre in Philadelphia we played when we played the theatre circuit. And that band I really learned to really
